incidents.title: Payment TLS expiry caused 502 errors
incidents.summary: Payment authorization failed with SSLHandshakeException for partner-bank, producing 502 responses from api-gateway for Globex, Hooli, Stark, etc. The failures ran from 09:14:00 to 09:27:09 on 15 Jul 2026 and stopped after the truststore was reloaded at 09:27:10.

causes.why: Warnings at L45040, L312279 and L580238 report the certificate expiring at 09:14:00; the first error logs appear exactly at 09:14:00 (L660873, L660874, L660875) with SSLHandshakeException indicating validity check failure, matching the expiry time.

causes.cause: Retry attempts amplified load on failing calls
causes.why: Repeated WARN lines L660876 show retry attempts (2/3) after the initial failures, but they occur after the root cause and do not explain the SSL error itself.

incidents.impact: All tenants saw POST /api/payments return 502, totaling 3,970 failed requests.
fix: Renew or replace the partner‑bank TLS certificate before its notAfter timestamp
Configure automated monitoring and alerts for certificate expiry to trigger pre‑emptive renewal
Ensure truststore reloads automatically when a new certificate is deployed

incidents.title: order-service DB transaction failures after v5.4.0 deploy
incidents.summary: A surge of CannotCreateTransactionException errors in order-service caused 503 responses from api-gateway for GET /api/orders and POST /api/checkout between 10:41:10 and 11:02:59 UTC. The incident ended when the order-service deployment was rolled back to version 5.3.2 at 11:01:40 UTC.

causes.cause: order-service version 5.4.0 introduced a DB connection pool exhaustion leading to transaction failures
causes.why: The deployment of order-service 5.4.0 occurred at 10:38:12 (line 1425003) shortly before the first WARN and ERROR logs at 10:41:10 (lines 1451580,1451581). The WARN about HikariPool timeout and the subsequent CannotCreateTransactionException errors appear immediately after the new version rollout, indicating the change caused the pool exhaustion.

causes.cause: Insufficient DB connections caused by high load
causes.why: WARN logs from postgres show long query durations (line 1432106) and the HikariPool timeout warnings (line 1451580) suggest the DB could not keep up, but these symptoms follow the version change and are not directly shown as a root cause.

incidents.impact: Eight tenants saw 503 errors – 4864 GET /api/orders and 4784 POST /api/checkout requests failed.
fix: Monitor HikariPool metrics after future deployments to catch connection saturation early
Add a pre‑deployment health check that validates DB connection pool availability
If similar errors appear, roll back the offending service version promptly, as done at line 1665084

incidents.title: Redis primary failover caused cache timeouts
incidents.summary: Cache reads timed out across cart, inventory, and search services from 12:22:00 to 12:28:22 after the primary Redis node went down. The incident ended when services reconnected to the new primary at 12:29:22.

causes.cause: Primary Redis node went down triggering a failover
causes.why: Sentinel logged the primary as down (+sdown at 12:22:05 L2381755, +odown at 12:22:09 L2382310) and then switched master to a new address (+switch-master at 12:22:41 L2387017). After this, all services logged RedisCommandTimeoutExceptions and reconnect warnings until they reconnected to the new primary.

incidents.impact: Eight tenants experienced failed requests (≈2,000 errors) due to cache read timeouts.
fix: Add health‑checks and alert on Sentinel +sdown/+odown events to trigger faster failover handling
Configure client retry/back‑off settings to reduce timeout spikes during master switches
Ensure the new primary is added to service discovery immediately and verify that all pods reload connection strings on sentinel events

incidents.title: notification-service offsets fail due to poll timeout
incidents.summary: From 14:05:00 to 14:21:58 the notification-service saw repeated offset‑commit failures, consumer‑poll timeouts and high lag across 8 tenants. The incident ended after a config reload at 14:21:30 that lowered max.poll.records, after which errors tapered off.

causes.cause: Long email send latency caused poll loops to exceed max.poll.interval.ms, triggering consumer timeouts, rebalances and offset‑commit failures
causes.why: WARN SMTP send slow entries (L3296910) appear at the start of the window, followed by WARN poll timeout messages (L3296918) and high lag warnings (L3297273). The same window contains 817 offset‑commit errors (L3296858, L3450109), indicating the timeout cascaded into commit failures.

incidents.impact: Eight tenants experienced failed Kafka offset commits (817 errors) and high consumer lag, preventing order‑event processing.
fix: Investigate and optimise EmailSender latency or increase max.poll.interval.ms to accommodate processing time.
Monitor consumer lag and poll timeout metrics; alert if poll timeout rate exceeds threshold.
Review recent config changes; ensure max.poll.records aligns with processing capacity before deployment.

incidents.title: Search API 503 due to OOM in search-service
incidents.summary: The search-service ran out of heap memory causing OOM kills and CrashLoopBackOff, which left api-gateway without a healthy upstream and returned 503 to clients from 15:40:54 to 15:52:58. The incident ended when a new image was rolled out at 15:52:05.

causes.cause: Search-service OOM leading to container crash
causes.why: Multiple OOM errors appear: WARN GC pauses start at 15:31 (L4063235), heap usage warnings at 15:31:23 (L4066628), then OutOfMemoryError errors from 15:40:57 (L4151584) and repeated OOMKilled warnings from kubelet at 15:41:36 (L4157331, L4157332). These indicate the JVM ran out of heap, killing the pod and causing upstream failures.

After the search-service crashes, api-gateway logs 503 errors citing "no healthy upstream" starting at 15:40:54 (L4151040) and continuing until the rollout, showing the symptom of the upstream failure.

incidents.impact: Clients received 503 on GET /api/search, 2413 failures across 8 tenants.
fix: Increase search-service heap size or tune GC to prevent full G1 pauses.

incidents.title: Checkout 409s caused by inventory deadlocks
incidents.summary: Inventory-service failed to reserve stock, returning 409 to checkout requests from 17:08 to 17:18 UTC. The issue affected 8 tenants and 1405 checkout calls. It ended when the inventory deployment rolled out a new image at 17:18:40.

causes.cause: Flash‑sale campaign spiked reservation traffic causing DB deadlocks
causes.why: The flash‑sale start log at 17:08:00 (L4924937) coincides with the first inventory errors (L4924982) and a flood of deadlock messages from Postgres (L4925035). The sudden load likely created competing updates on the same inventory rows, leading to the observed CannotAcquireLockException and deadlocks.

causes.cause: PostgreSQL deadlock detection propagates as CannotAcquireLockException
causes.why: Each inventory error includes a nested PSQLException reporting "ERROR: deadlock detected" (L4924982, L4925030) and the postgres log records the same deadlock (L4925035). This directly explains the reservation failures.

incidents.impact: Customers received 409 Conflict on POST /api/checkout – 1405 occurrences across 8 tenants.
fix: Add exponential back‑off and retry logic for inventory reservations in order-service
Review and tune PostgreSQL lock settings and batch size to reduce contention during flash‑sale periods
Implement monitoring alerts for deadlock count spikes and throttle checkout traffic when thresholds are exceeded
